nodes.summary: Inequalities for the correlations of ferromagnetic Ising models: the Griffiths (GKS) and FKG inequalities, monotonicity in the couplings and the temperature, and the Griffiths–Hurst–Sherman inequality with its consequences for the magnetization.
nodes.title: Correlation inequalities for spin systems

nodes.summary: Exact results for the two-dimensional Ising model: Kramers–Wannier duality between high- and low-temperature expansions, and Onsager's formula for the free energy through Kac–Ward determinants, Sherman's loop identities and the homology of the torus.
nodes.title: Exact solutions and duality

nodes.summary: Infinite-volume states of the Ising model and its phase transition: weak limits of box measures and the DLR condition, translation invariance, ergodicity and extremality of the plus state, spontaneous magnetization and the critical temperature, and Peierls' contour argument for long-range order.
nodes.title: Gibbs states and phase transitions

nodes.summary: The random-cluster (Fortuin–Kasteleyn) model and its Edwards–Sokal coupling with the Potts and Ising models: finite-volume measures, the FKG inequality and comparison with Bernoulli percolation, infinite-volume limits, translation invariance and ergodicity, the free energy, agreement of free and wired measures, and the critical point.
nodes.title: Random-cluster model

nodes.summary: The random-current representation of Ising correlations and the switching lemma, and the sharpness of the Ising phase transition: the Simon–Lieb inequality, exponential decay of correlations below the critical point and the mean-field lower bound on the magnetization above it.
nodes.title: Random currents and sharpness

nodes.summary: Spin models on finite graphs: the Ising Hamiltonian, Gibbs distribution and partition function and their agreement with the canonical ensemble, the pressure and its independence of boundary conditions, and the Lee–Yang theorem on the zeros of the partition function.
nodes.title: Lattice spin models

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
